headline: Fastest send: short beta, 1.6s under average
summary: You sent The Green Slab in 11.8s on the shortest beta of the session, skipping 7 holds to keep things clean. Your right foot anchored on hold 2 for nearly half the climb, letting the other limbs move freely. The one wobble was a 1.8s read between hold 15 and your left foot's move to 10.

strengths.title: Shortest beta of session
strengths.detail: You skipped 7 of 16 holds, cutting readjustments and finishing 1.6s faster than your session average. Fewer touches kept the climb crisp.

strengths.title: Stable right-foot anchor
strengths.detail: Hold 2 carried your right foot for 4.61s, anchoring the body while hands and left foot cycled through the middle section.

strengths.title: Clean matched-hand transitions
strengths.detail: Both hands shared holds 7, 10, 12, and 16, giving you natural rest points without breaking rhythm.

focus.title: 1.8s read mid-climb
focus.detail: No new placement between 6.80s and 8.63s while your right hand sat on 15. Scanning the next move from the ground would close this gap.

focus.title: Left foot hanging 21%
focus.detail: Your left foot was off a hold for nearly a quarter of the climb, shifting load to the arms. Placing it earlier keeps tension balanced.

drills.name: Pre-scan from ground
drills.how: Before stepping on, walk the route from the floor and call out each hand and foot placement. This shrinks in-climb reading pauses.

drills.name: Foot-first movement
drills.how: Drill moves where the foot lands before the hand reaches. This trains the habit of placing feet early to reduce arm load.

beta: Keep the 9-hold line (7, 1, 2, 10, 12, 5, 6, 15, 16) but pre-place the left foot on 10 before the right hand commits to 15 to eliminate the mid-climb pause.
next_goal: Send the same 9-hold beta in under 10.5s with the left foot on a hold 85%+ of the time.
